response.sql: WITH cust AS (SELECT CustomerId, SUM(Total) AS total_spent FROM Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId), shares AS (SELECT CustomerId, total_spent, total_spent * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(total_spent) FROM cust) AS share FROM cust), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS a FROM shares), kept AS (SELECT s.* FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share WHERE s.share > avg_share.a) SELECT AVG(k.total_spent) AS avg_total_spent, AVG(k.share) AS avg_share, AVG((k.share - avg_share.a) / avg_share.a) AS avg_relative_difference FROM kept k CROSS JOIN avg_share;

assumptions.assumption: Each customer's total spend is the sum of Invoice.Total over their invoices, and only customers with at least one invoice are in the population. Shares use the sum of those totals as the denominator, and the average share is the unweighted mean across those customers.
Customer totals are taken from the Invoice.Total column, not recomputed from InvoiceLine.UnitPrice times Quantity. No rounding is applied, as requested.

alternatives.interpretation: Include every customer in the population, including customers with no invoices (total spend 0), so the average share and the share denominator are computed across all customers in the Customer table.
alternatives.sql: WITH cust AS (SELECT c.CustomerId, COALESCE(SUM(i.Total), 0) AS total_spent FROM Customer c LEFT JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId), shares AS (SELECT CustomerId, total_spent, total_spent * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(total_spent) FROM cust) AS share FROM cust), avg_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS a FROM shares), kept AS (SELECT s.* FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share WHERE s.share > avg_share.a) SELECT AVG(k.total_spent) AS avg_total_spent, AVG(k.share) AS avg_share, AVG((k.share - avg_share.a) / avg_share.a) AS avg_relative_difference FROM kept k CROSS JOIN avg_share;
